_about: The campaign's registry: every run, read-out and exhibit, which experiment it belongs to, what it is for and whether it is still valid. agent/results/ is laid out from it (one folder per experiment), the indexes and reports are generated from it, and tools/campaign.py check fails when something is missing. Register a run BEFORE launching it (RUNBOOK, definition of done).

groups.title: E1 — the main comparison: DiscoPoP alone vs DiscoPoP + agent
groups.question: Where DiscoPoP alone reaches no verified parallel program (class R), does the agent — the same DiscoPoP and gate plus a model that restructures — deliver correct speedups? Does it do no harm where DiscoPoP already succeeds (class A), and decline true recurrences (class D)? Does anything wrong get through? (H1, H2, H4)
groups.headline: TSVC class R: the agent reaches a verified parallel program in 46 of 90 trials and is FASTER in 44; DiscoPoP alone in 0 of 90 (Wilcoxon p = 0.002, Cliff's δ +0.50). 0 unsafe in 288 trials with a verdict. Class D: 12 of 12 correctly declined. Class A: 1 better, 1 worse, 1 lost — the reason for proposal D32. [D36, 23 Sep: the TSVC sources named the solving transformation in their header — these TSVC agent numbers are 'with the hint'; the clean three-way redo is E1c (e1c_r_1–4, e1c_a, e1c_d).]

groups.title: E1-bare — the same model with no DiscoPoP and no gate
groups.question: What does the pipeline add over handing the program to the same model and asking it to parallelize it? The bare arm's BROKEN count is what the gate prevents; its FASTER count is what DiscoPoP's evidence and the gate's feedback add.
groups.headline: TSVC class R, 18 loops × 5, the same model with no DiscoPoP and no gate: FASTER in 58 of 88 trials, 53 of them race-free by the gate's own TSan and schedule matrix (4 benign races on s293, 1 not judgeable) — more than the agent's 44 of 90 (DiscoPoP alone: 0 of 90) — but a WRONG program shipped in 17 (19 %, all 17 stopped by the gate when replayed) and a slower one in 12, where the agent shipped 0 of either. Over the model, the pipeline adds trust, not reach — and most of the reach it loses is lost after the model: Phase B's speed check judges pragmas one at a time and drops sets that only pay together (7 trials recoverable, D33 proposed), the gate's clause stage falsely rejects one half of s281's split (5), DiscoPoP cannot write s331's reduction(max); the rest are rewrites that are slow in themselves. Agent v2 (D32, D33, Fixes 91–92, built the same evening) replayed on E1's archived trials and verified by the harness: FASTER in 55 of 90, 0 unsafe — no longer behind the model alone's 53. [D36: 'with the hint in the source' and the contract prompt (D37) — superseded by the clean model-alone arm in e2_ab_clean_a/b; d36_hint_check measures the hint.] [Superseded as the model-alone reference by E1c's bare_llm (the mirror prompt, D37; the packages without the hint, D36): 44 FASTER, 39 race-free, 46 of 90 unusable.]

groups.title: E1 clean — the three-way main comparison on clean packages (D35, D36)
groups.question: On TSVC class R, with no hint in the source (D36), the model confined to its workspace (Fix 95) and agent v2: DiscoPoP alone vs DiscoPoP + agent (`default`) vs the model alone (`bare_llm`, the mirror prompt, D37) — which delivers correct, race-free, faster programs, and which ships wrong or slower ones? Plus the no-harm (class A) and must-decline (class D) controls.
groups.headline: TSVC class R, clean packages, agent v2, the model alone with the mirror prompt, 18 loops × 5: DiscoPoP alone reaches nothing (0 of 90); the agent is FASTER in 51 of 90, all race-free, and ships 0 unusable programs; the model alone is FASTER in 44, race-free in 39, and ships 46 unusable programs of 90 (16 BROKEN, 17 slower, 8 not compiling, 5 racy). H13 supported (agent fewer unusable on 14 loops, 0 the other way, p = 0.0004); reach: agent ahead on 10 loops, the model alone on 4, not significant (p = 0.13). Agent vs DiscoPoP alone: gained 51, unsafe 0, p = 0.0002. Controls: class A — agent equal to DiscoPoP alone (3.63× v 3.67×), model alone 1 of 3 not compiling; class D — agent declined 12 of 12, model alone 9 of 12 unusable (6 BROKEN).

groups.title: E2 — evidence, feedback and model strength
groups.question: On TSVC class R, does DiscoPoP's evidence raise the model's success rate (H5), more for Haiku than for Sonnet? Does the gate's failure feedback partly substitute for it (H5b)? Where must the evidence come from (none, compiler remarks, where the time goes, DiscoPoP), which part of it matters, and which part of the prompt? Runs on agent v2 with its own default arm (D34).
groups.headline: E2 A+B (Haiku, TSVC class R, 18 × 5, with D38 twins): DiscoPoP's evidence adds nothing — H12, H5b, H5d not supported (evidence effect −0.03 inside the pipeline, −0.02 on the twins); the best arm is the agent without evidence at 3 attempts (55 of 90 race-free FASTER). H13 supported everywhere: every agent arm 0 unusable programs, its twins 71 of 90 and 73 of 89, the model alone 46; DiscoPoP's own pragmas unchecked (twin_dp) wrong in 70 of 90. Sonnet cells, evidence-source arms, Parts C/D to run.

groups.title: Agent v3 pilot (D40) — the speed verdict inside the model's budget
groups.question: Does D40 — a kept rewrite's pragmas judged in Phase A (safety, then timed against the program before it) with the failure fed back while the region's budget lasts, and the prompt stating the deciding comparison — raise the race-free FASTER rate on the ten class-R loops where v2's results varied? And, with it, does DiscoPoP's evidence start to matter (default vs no_evidence)? Decides whether E1c's and E2's agent arms are rerun under v3.
groups.preregistered: Written before any trial (26 Sep). Loops: s112, s121, s1213, s211, s212, s241, s243, s244, s252, s281. Arms default and no_evidence (budget 3), Haiku, x3 each: 60 trials, agent v3 (--judge-as-shipped). Baseline, v2 on the same loops: default 21 of 50 race-free FASTER (E1c), no_evidence 25 of 50 (E2). Expectation: both v3 arms above their v2 baseline, because the trials v2 lost here were correct rewrites lost on speed after the model's turn (why_trials_fail.md). Read-out: rate per arm vs its baseline (descriptive — a pilot), D40 verdicts (ok / not_faster / pattern_broken), model calls per trial, and whether no_evidence still leads default.

groups.title: E10 — does the speed check keep unnecessary changes out?
groups.question: With the speed check timed at a size where speed is measurable, are correct-but-not-faster changes kept out without lowering the delivered speedup? (H10, H10b) Decided D22.
groups.headline: The speed check ON at the kernel's timing size is the only configuration with no unsafe acceptance and nothing below DiscoPoP alone (D22).

groups.title: E11 — against RepoOMP on its NPB-C kernels
groups.question: On identical programs and verification, are the agent's results verified correct at least as often as RepoOMP's released outputs? (H11)

groups.title: T0.1 — size calibration
groups.question: At which size is each benchmark's serial computation long enough to verify (≥ 1 s) and to time (≥ 0.25 s)?

groups.title: T0.2 — DiscoPoP profile stability
groups.question: Is DiscoPoP's profile the same every time?

groups.title: T0.3 — can the correctness oracle see a wrong program?
groups.question: Replaying every candidate the gate ever judged through the harness verification.

groups.title: T0.4 — timing noise on a shared host
groups.question: What speedup can the loaded server resolve, and do concurrent lanes interfere?

groups.title: T0.5 — runtime share per region
groups.question: Where does each benchmark's time go, and what does a runtime-share floor cost?

groups.title: T0.6 — DiscoPoP's patterns inside main
groups.question: Does DiscoPoP on its own propose pragmas inside main (decision D4)?

groups.title: T0.7 — DiscoPoP's explorer on one profile
groups.question: Is DiscoPoP's explorer deterministic on a fixed profile?

groups.title: T0.8 — packaging equivalence (D6)
groups.question: Does DiscoPoP see the same program in the project layout as in the merged file?

groups.title: T0.9 — fast refresh vs full profile over chains of rewrites
groups.question: Over successive rewrites, does a fast refresh reach the conclusions a full re-profile reaches — and where not, is the divergence the dangerous kind (a suggestion the measured profile does not support)?
groups.headline: 23 Sep (after D29): 11 of 18 comparisons identical, 7 produce a suggestion the measured profile does not support (18 Sep: 8 / 8 / 2 lost).

groups.title: T0.10 — expert references
groups.question: Is there, for every restructuring benchmark, an expert version that is correct AND faster?

groups.title: T0.11 — the measured class of every benchmark
groups.question: Does DiscoPoP alone reach a verified parallel program (class A), never (R), or never on a true recurrence (D)?

groups.title: T0.13 — the default arm's ceiling
groups.question: Can the pipeline KEEP a perfect rewrite: the expert restructuring with its pragmas stripped, no model?

groups.title: T0.14 — reference acceptance
groups.question: Does each package accept its own expert version? A BROKEN there is a defect of the package.

groups.title: Benchmark suitability audit (§5k, D18)
groups.question: DiscoPoP + gate alone on every benchmark, no model: which benchmarks can show the contribution at all?

groups.title: Pilots (before the campaign's design was fixed)
groups.question: The first agent runs; they decided D9 (the E1 model) and exposed the defects fixed before E1.

groups.title: Harness and pipeline checks (not experiments)
groups.question: Smokes and observed runs that tested the harness, the packaging and the agent end to end.

groups.question: Launcher logs and diagnostic logs kept for reference.

bare_s241_r2_distribution_reads_new_a_br.shows: s241 distributed so that b[i] = a[i]*a[i+1]*d[i] reads the NEW a[i+1] where the original read the old one.

bare_s243_r3_distribution_reads_new_a_br.shows: s243 split into three parallel loops; the third reads a[i+1] already overwritten by the first.

bare_s244_r4_distribution_wrong_order_br.shows: s244 distributed in an order that lets the dead store a[i+1] = … survive where the original overwrites it.

bare_s1213_r2_snapshot_never_read_broken.shows: The model alone fills a snapshot a_old to break s1213's anti-dependence — and then reads the live a[i+1]: the fix is written and not used.

bare_s112_r1_pragma_on_recurrence_broken.shows: A bare '#pragma omp parallel for' on s112's backward recurrence a[i+1] = a[i] + b[i]: a WAR race, 3.8× faster and wrong.

bare_s112_r3_pragma_on_recurrence_broken.shows: The same racy pragma on s112 in a second repeat.

bare_s241_r1_race_kept_in_loop_broken.shows: Reading a[i+1] into a local first does not remove the race: another thread may already have written it.

bare_s1213_r4_jacobi_for_gauss_seidel_br.shows: Double-buffering s1213 turns a Gauss–Seidel update into a Jacobi one — the seidel-2d error of the first smoke, in a TSVC loop.

bare_s241_r3_snapshot_before_pb_mix_brok.shows: A snapshot of a taken before pb_mix changes the input: two stale elements per repetition, dump error 0.93 — a subtle error only a full-output check finds.

bare_s252_r3_prefix_scan_wrong_algorithm.shows: The model alone replaces s252's two-term sum with a full prefix scan: a different algorithm, wrong and 0.1× slow.

bare_s341_r2_compaction_order_lost_broke.shows: A compaction whose index comes from a critical counter: the packed order depends on thread timing, and the run then fails.

bare_s281_index_split_5of5_faster.shows: Where the agent got 0 of 5, the model alone wins s281 in 5 of 5 by splitting the index range at LEN/2 — no copy, 3.0× at 12 threads.

bare_s331_max_reduction_5of5_faster.shows: s331 won 5 of 5 by the model alone with reduction(max: j) — the pragma DiscoPoP cannot write, so the agent (DiscoPoP writes its pragmas, D23) cannot reach it.

bare_s121_parallel_copy_faster.shows: s121: the model alone buffers a like the agent did, but copies it with a PARALLEL loop — 1.6× where the agent's memcpy version ran at 0.73×.

bare_s244_dead_store_removed_faster.shows: s244: the model alone sees that a[i+1] = … is overwritten by the next iteration except at the last, keeps only that one, and the loop becomes parallel — 3.6×.

bare_s112_r5_copy_per_repetition_worse.shows: A correct program shipped 7× SLOWER than the original (malloc + memcpy of a per repetition): without Settle, a slower program is delivered as parallelized.
